newsitem.title: UK: Siebe ends up but strong stg clouds 1996.
newsitem.headline: Siebe ends up but strong stg clouds 1996.

text.p: Shares in international engineering group Siebe Plc rose on Tuesday following good first half results and analysts remained upbeat on the stock despite the negative impact of strong sterling.
At the London close, Siebe shares were up 11-1/2p at 951-1/2p.
Analysts said the impact of sterling's strength would be more noticeable in the second half, although cost control efforts could provide some relief.
Analysts' forecasts for full-year pre-tax profits ranged from 415 to 430 million stg.
Taxable profits for the six months to September 30 rose to 190.4 million stg from 144.2 million a year ago on sales up 22 percent at 1.47 billion stg.
Lehman Brothers analyst Chris Heminway said there was no reason to change a full-year estimate of 415 million stg, although the currency effect in the second half will be more noticeable.
"The growth rate in the markets that they are serving is certainly under pressure at the moment and we anticipate it will remain so over the next 18 months," he added.
But he said that even if the rate of sales growth at Siebe slowed down they could still increase margins for a while.

Heminway and other analysts noted Siebe's efforts to boost productivity by controlling costs. "There's a slight change of emphasis I think in terms of where the profits growth is going to come from over the next couple of years," Heminway said.
Credit Lyonnais Laing analyst Daniel Bevan said the second half outlook looked encouraging, with a healthy order book for control systems, and productivity gains possible.
"I think growth in control systems will be slightly improved," Bevan said. But he, too, was cautious on the impact of the sterling-dollar exchange rate.
"We would have reduced first half profits by nine million stg had it not been for the exchange rate," he said.

Heminway saw a slowdown in growth in the control systems sector. "They have been gaining market share, but we just think it's going to be more difficult for them to continue to do that than it has been for some time historically."

"I don't think the stock is substantially undervalued. At the beginning of the year, there was a big discount to its best global competitors as we measured them and that discount has changed...and we think that undervaluation has been largely corrected," he said.

Another analyst, who declined to be named, said the first half results were in line with expectations. "The only fly in the ointment was that they saw an underlying slowdown in the controls market," he said.

"The company is on quite a high rating, so although in profit terms it will outperform its peer group, the fact that there has been a slowdown in key markets means that we are a little bit more cautious than we once were," he said.
Siebe said it will offset this by market share gains.
"It's not a cheap stock any more. It's had a great run. What'll probably happen is the share price will probably consolidate," the analyst said.
